What this run actually graded

Scope of this verdict

This run graded the LOCAL CHECKOUT of each member it could resolve, not the tree at the registry pin. Remote fetch-at-sha is deferred (ADR 0039, question 1). The pin, entry version and graded sha below are shown for every member, including the ones where they agree, so agreement is never inferred from silence.

What the columns mean

Standard debt counts findings held below their severity by that member's own Standard pin, whether the check postdates the pin or a tightening has not reached it yet: green-by-an-old-pin, made visible. Pin is what the catalogue advertises; Graded is the checkout this run actually read. They are shown for every member, including the ones where they agree.

03

Not graded, and why

The difference between a broken artifact and an incomplete workstation.

Two failures wear the word "unresolved", and only one is a red

An unresolvable entry is a defect in the catalogue: an installer following it receives nothing, so it reds the collection. A member not graded is a gap in this machine rather than in the artifact, and never reds.

  • NOT GRADEDdelta - no local checkout found for this member (looked in: delta); the entry is well-formed, so this is a gap in this machine, not in the catalogue
  • UNRESOLVABLEepsilon - local source "./members/epsilon" does not exist under /repos/example-catalogue; an installer following this entry gets nothing
